title: Decidability of local asymptotic stability for polynomial ODEs
decision_reason: Explicit rational-input local-asymptotic formulation, independent July 2026 corroboration, ten exact-scope comparisons, duplicate check, separated A50 review and final validation passed. No matching unresolved resolution claim located.
aliases: algorithmic local asymptotic stability of rational polynomial vector fields

problem_fingerprint.model: Autonomous continuous-time ODE x'=f(x) on R^n, f in Q[x_1,...,x_n]^n and f(0)=0.
problem_fingerprint.input: Finite exact binary encoding of n and all rational coefficients/monomial exponents; dimension and polynomial degree vary over finite inputs.
problem_fingerprint.solution: Unique maximal classical solution from each initial state. No promise of global existence away from the equilibrium's neighbourhood.
problem_fingerprint.stability: For every epsilon>0 there is delta>0 such that every solution with Euclidean norm of its initial state less than delta exists for all nonnegative times and remains inside the epsilon-ball.
problem_fingerprint.attraction: There is r>0 such that every solution starting in the r-ball exists for all nonnegative times and converges to zero.
problem_fingerprint.target: Does one Turing algorithm halt on every valid input and decide whether the origin is locally asymptotically stable, meaning both stability and local attraction?
problem_fingerprint.scope: No time-complexity bound, hyperbolicity promise, homogeneity assumption or gap from a stability boundary. A negative answer includes stable but nonattracting equilibria.
problem_fingerprint.canonical_scope: One local-asymptotic-stability decision problem. Homogeneous/fixed-degree cases and certificate existence are not separately counted.

statement_sources.locator: Section 2 definitions, Section 3 rational-input question and its explicit local-asymptotic version, Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 3.2.

independently_authored_corroboration.locator: Section I opening discussion; Section II model and complete Theorem II.2.
independently_authored_corroboration.independence: Liu–Fitzsimmons and Ahmadi–Parrilo are disjoint author teams.
independently_authored_corroboration.scope: Current paper retains algorithmic stability question while disproving a distinct polynomial-certificate converse.

second_review.arrangement: Primary-agent research followed by a separated adversarial self-pass; no independent agent or human review.
issues_found: The initial draft did not explicitly explain the decidability of the stronger exponential-stability property.
Searches surfaced stability-preserving quadratization and an asymptotic/exponential transformation title.
Negative output must include stable but nonattracting equilibria; degree-bound obstructions must not be mistaken for Turing undecidability.
issues_resolved: Read Corollary 3.3 and proof, and added its exact scope to the draft.
Read complete CP24 and J25 theorem statements with definitions: Hurwitz-Jacobian preservation and homotopy conditional on prior stability do not decide the candidate.

Checked exact rational encoding, all-neighbourhood quantifiers, local forward existence, separate attraction, arbitrary finite dimension/degree and no runtime bound. Draft consistently uses failure of local asymptotic stability.
second_review.quantifier_checks: One terminating Turing algorithm for all finite rational polynomial inputs; all real initial states in the quantified neighbourhoods; no global forward-completeness, homogeneity or hyperbolicity promise. Polynomial local Lipschitzness provides unique maximal solutions.
second_review.application_check: Foundational verification of an already specified polynomial model. No efficient controller synthesis or automatic transfer from a polynomial approximation.
second_review.duplicate_check: Full nearest statements read again; refreshed aliases across active pages, metadata, candidate records and exclusions. No duplicate located.
second_review.search_limit: Generic numerical-solver, periodic-orbit, special-model and namesake hits were not treated as openness evidence. Exact correction queries returned substantial unrelated results.

nearest_existing.comparison: Discrete-time products of finitely many rational matrices, quantified over every switching sequence, at a strict spectral-radius threshold. This candidate concerns one autonomous continuous-time nonlinear vector field and local stability plus attraction.
Generic existence of a static output-feedback gain at the critical dimension, across input/output dimensions. It does not ask for a total decision procedure for nonlinear polynomial equilibria.

Whether a specified trajectory of a rational linear ODE hits a hyperplane. The candidate instead quantifies over an entire neighbourhood and tests stability and attraction for a nonlinear equilibrium.

source_records.title: Revisiting the Complexity of Stability of Continuous and Hybrid Systems
source_records.version: v1 April 28, 2014; v2 May 1; v3 May 11; v4 June 4, 2014. Regenerated June 2021 PDF date not treated as revision.

source_records.title: Dissipative quadratizations of polynomial ODE systems
source_records.version: v1 November 4, 2023; v2 January 24, 2024. Cited v2 author preprint; arXiv records TACAS 2024 publication.
source_records.read: Dissipativity here means a Hurwitz Jacobian at an equilibrium. The transformation preserves that property; it does not decide general local asymptotic stability.

source_records.title: Asymptotic stability equals exponential stability—while you twist your eyes
source_records.version: Author manuscript dated May 30, 2025. Filename not used as publication date.
source_records.locator: Full §1.3 stability definitions; Assumption 3.5; complete Theorem 3.6 and proof.
source_records.read: For a smooth manifold of dimension other than five, two locally Lipschitz fields sharing a globally asymptotically stable equilibrium have a homotopy of semiflows preserving that property. Stability is a hypothesis, not decided from rational polynomial input.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Strong NP-hardness already for homogeneous cubic fields; linear systems admit a polynomial-time decision.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Hardness does not preclude all terminating algorithms, while the linear restriction excludes the nonlinear input class.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Stable integer-coefficient cubic example with no local real-analytic Lyapunov function and with an explicit rational certificate.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Eliminates a particular certificate family, not every possible exact algorithm for the stability decision.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Existential certificate degrees for homogeneous fields; no dimension-and-degree-only bound in the stated real-parameter family.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: No guaranteed finite stopping on negative instances and no general nonhomogeneous decision procedure. The degree-bound obstruction is not an undecidability proof for rational inputs.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Global asymptotic stability of a discrete-time rational ReLU-feedback system is undecidable.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Discrete time, piecewise affine feedback and global target differ from a continuous-time polynomial field and local target. No transfer to the candidate is established by this theorem.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Finite-time blow-up/maximal-interval boundedness of a specified trajectory for polynomial differential equations.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: A different observable and input/coefficient presentation; no equivalence to stability plus attraction of an equilibrium neighbourhood is supplied.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Bounded delta-decision algorithms and unbounded arithmetic-hierarchy upper classifications in a broader computable-function language.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Positive tolerance and bounded quantifiers do not decide the exact all-time property. Broad-class membership or undecidability does not supply hardness for rational polynomial fields.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Truncated SOS certificate search followed by exact rational recovery, with explicit failure outputs.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Failure to find a certificate at the supplied degree does not decide that the equilibrium fails local asymptotic stability.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Local exponential stability is decided by the Jacobian. Earlier algebraic-unsolvability examples have a non-semialgebraic parameter locus.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Asymptotic convergence need not be exponential. Failure of a finite semialgebraic characterization is not by itself Turing undecidability.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Preserves strict negativity of Jacobian eigenvalue real parts under a quadratic lifting.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Does not classify nonhyperbolic equilibria or supply a total local-asymptotic-stability test.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Existential homotopy between systems already assumed globally asymptotically stable.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: No effective test of the stability hypothesis, no finite rational-polynomial transformation supplied for all inputs, and no negative-instance stopping rule.
